# SPE Round 5 Plan: Invoice Extraction Agent

The user's prompt for this round is "go again", with the r04 log, F9 and the r04 proposals pasted above it. This plan respecs from that evidence.

The r04 lines I was given show only the field accuracy metric. So this round predicts field accuracy plus two new subset rows that test F9 and R's r04 Why. I also assume spec.md ended at requirement R30, so new IDs start at R31. If spec.md already uses R31, I will shift the numbers when I write the file. Requirement IDs (R31 and up) are not the same thing as config R.

## 1. Specify

### Proposals from r04

| ID | Proposal | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | Keep OCR cleanup but skip it on two-column layouts | Adopt as new config S | F9 is open. S changes one thing from R, which is the layout gate. Config R stays in the run so any difference between R and S comes from the gate. |
| P2 | Add 15 scanned invoices with handwriting | Reject for r05 and log as an open decision | Q measured 0.93, which is not a ceiling. The ceiling rule applies only when every config hits the maximum. Changing the eval set and a config in the same round would break comparison with r04. The new invoices also need reference fields from the AP lead, and only the user can arrange that. |
| P3 | Drop config P | Adopt | P trails Q on every r04 metric, so another P run costs tokens and gives no new information. Q becomes the baseline. P's r04 rows stay in the log. |

### Requirements added in r05

All r04 requirements stay in force unless a row below changes them.

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R31 | The r05 configs are Q, R and S. P is retired, and its row stays with the note "retired r05, P3". | P3 adopted | The harness config list equals ["Q","R","S"]. |
| R32 | S is config R with OCR cleanup skipped on every invoice that S's layout check marks as two-column. Nothing else changes from R. | r04 F9, P1 | Config diff check: S and R differ only in the gate flag. The tool-call log shows zero cleanup calls by S on invoices that S marks as two-column. |
| R33 | S's line-item recall on two-column invoices is at least Q's recall minus 0.02. | r04 F9 | Grader check `line_item_recall[layout=two_column]` |
| R34 | S's layout check agrees with the frozen layout tags on at least 57 of the 60 invoices. | P1 depends on correct detection | Grader check `layout_tag_agreement` |

| R36 | Report total accuracy on scanned invoices for Q, R and S. | r04 miss on R ("OCR cleanup fixes scanned totals") | Grader check `total_exact[scanned=true]` |

### Defaults and open decisions

| Item | Default this round | Reason |
|---|---|---|

The work affected is the eval set and the AP lead's time. The user decides. | Only the user can commit the AP lead's time. |

## 2. Predict

Q and R start from their r04 measured values because they are unchanged. The naive column is the r04 measured value. For S it is R's value, because S is R plus one change.

| Metric | Grader check | Q | R | S | Naive (Q / R / S) | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field accuracy, all 60 | `field_exact_rate` | 0.93 ± 0.03 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.93 ± 0.03 | 0.93 / 0.88 / 0.88 | Q and R are unchanged from r04. The gate makes S treat two-column invoices like Q does. R's scanned-total gain is unproven, so I add nothing to S for it. |
| Line-item recall, two-column subset | `line_item_recall[layout=two_column]` | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.60 ± 0.15 | 0.92 ± 0.05 | none (new row) | New row. F9 shows that cleanup drops line items on these invoices. S skips cleanup on these invoices, so it should match Q. R's band is wide because I have no r04 count for this subset. |
| Total accuracy, scanned subset | `total_exact[scanned=true]` | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.90 ± 0.08 | 0.90 ± 0.08 | none (new row) | New row. It tests R's r04 Why directly. S keeps cleanup on single-column scans, so it should match R. If R does not beat Q here, cleanup has no measured benefit, and I will propose removing it in r06. |

Stop check: r04 had a miss, so the run of matched rounds is 0. The loop cannot stop after r05.

## 3. Evaluate

### After approval, in this order

1. Save the user's prompt and "go again" word for word to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`.
2. Append the r05 requirement table to `spe/spec/spec.md`. Mark P as retired. Add the defaults table and the P2 row to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`.
3. Commit with the subject `spe r05: specify`.
4. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` from the Predict table, including the bands, the grader checks and the naive values. After a trial runs, nobody edits the YAML.
5. Commit with the subject `spe r05: predict`.
6. Build config S. Add the two-column gate at the OCR cleanup call site behind a config flag. Then add a unit test. On a two-column fixture, the test asserts that cleanup is not called. On a single-column scan fixture, it asserts that cleanup is called.
7. Write the tag script and `spe/evals/subsets/r05-tags.csv`. Freeze the file and record its hash in the run manifest.

### Gates (each must pass before the next one starts)

| Gate | Pass condition | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| Grader selftest | `field_exact_rate`, the new `line_item_recall` and `total_exact` subset checks, and `layout_tag_agreement` all return the known answers on fixtures. | Halt and report. The grader is broken. |
| Control regrade of r04 | Regrading the saved r04 outputs reproduces Q 0.93 and R 0.88 field accuracy exactly. The new subset checks also run on r04 outputs, but those numbers are for information only. | Halt and report. The grader has drifted. |
| Eval set check | The eval set hash equals the r04 hash. No config's prompt or tool reads the reference fields. | Halt and report a possible leaked answer key. |
| Dry run | 2 invoices × 3 configs, with at least 1 two-column invoice. Outputs parse. Tool logs exist. S makes no cleanup call on the two-column invoice. | Fix the harness and rerun the dry run. Predictions stay as they are. |

### Workflow launch

Script: `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js`. It is a copy of the r04 script with the config list, the tag file and the new grader checks updated.

```json
{
  "round": "r05",
  "configs": ["Q", "R", "S"],
  "model": "Sonnet 5.5",
  "evalSet": "spe/evals/sets/invoices-60",
  "tags": "spe/evals/subsets/r05-tags.csv",
  "predictions": "spe/predictions/r05.yaml",
  "trialsPerInvoice": 1,
  "concurrency": 6,
  "budgetTokens": 7000000,
  "out": "spe/evals/results/r05/"
}
```

I chose the eval set and results paths to match the spe/ layout. If the r04 script uses other paths, I will use the r04 paths.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

The run is 180 trials. I estimate about 15k input tokens and 2k output tokens per trial. That is about 2.7M input tokens and 0.4M output tokens, plus the dry run. Wall time is about 30 to 45 minutes at a concurrency of 6. The budget cap is 7M tokens, which is about twice the estimate. The run halts at the cap.

### After the run

1. Append the r05 section to `spe/prediction-log.md`. It gets one row per metric and config with the predicted value, the measured value, the naive value, hit or miss, and which of the prediction or the naive value came closer.
2. Update F9 in `spe/failures.md` with the r05 result. If the gate also misroutes invoices, log that as a new F-number.
3. Commit with the subject `spe r05: evaluate`.
4. In the learn step, write "Proposed for round 6" in spec.md. Then commit with the subject `spe r05: learn`.

### Halt and report

- The budget cap is reached.
- The grader selftest or the control regrade fails.
- The eval set hash changed, or any config could read the reference fields.
- Any decision needs the user, such as P2.
- This loop never pushes, deploys or sends anything. Commits stay local, and they carry no Claude attribution lines.
